drake.name: Drake Passage
drake.note: Narrowest ACC choke point; strongest flow, roughest seas

pacific.name: SE Pacific ACC
pacific.note: Open Pacific sector, far from land

chile.name: Offshore southern Chile
chile.note: Near-shore stage control; sits north of the ACC core

drake.title: Sea temperature at pod depth
drake.assumption: 4.0 C at 150 m, slider range 0.0-10.0 C
drake.finding: Observed median 1.2 C, colder than the 4.0 C default; 85% of profiles fall inside the slider range. Colder sea helps heat rejection, so a warm default is the conservative side.
drake.sim_change: Set the default sea temperature to about 1.2 C for this site; keep the 0-10 C range.
sources: Argo float profiles, Ifremer ERDDAP ArgoFloats (erddap.ifremer.fr), QC flag 1

drake.title: Current speed at pod depth
drake.finding: Median 0.16 m/s (P5 0.05, P95 0.51); 5.0% of 3-hourly samples are below 0.05 m/s; direction steadiness 0.57 (1 = one-way flow).
drake.sim_change: Add this site's P5/P50/P95 as presets on the current slider; model slack water as a first-class case.
sources: HYCOM GLBy0.08 expt 93.0 analysis, THREDDS NCSS (tds.hycom.org); a model, not observations

drake.title: Seawater volumetric heat capacity
drake.assumption: rho*cp = 4.1 MJ/m3/K; nu = 1.56e-6 m2/s in the Reynolds readout
drake.finding: TEOS-10 gives rho*cp = 4.099 MJ/m3/K at 1.2 C (0.0% from the sim). Kinematic viscosity is 1.78e-6 m2/s, so the Reynolds readout is 12% high.
drake.sim_change: Change the Reynolds readout to use nu = 1.62e-6 m2/s at 4 C (minor).
sources: Churchill-Bernstein / Churchill-Chu correlations; Sharqawy et al. 2010 seawater properties; TEOS-10 (gsw)

drake.title: Hull heat-transfer coefficient U
drake.finding: Still-water U matches (242 vs 200) because turbulent natural convection is strong at a 25 K wall-sea difference, but the sim's slope is too steep: at 0.5 m/s physics gives 323 against 800, since the glycol side, steel wall and fouling cap U at about 612 W/m2K and the outside film is no longer the only resistance. Worst sim/physics ratio across P10-P90 currents is 2.2x.
drake.sim_change: Replace the sim's U with a curve fitted to the physics: roughly 242 W/m2K still rising to 323 at 0.5 m/s. Inner-side h and fouling are my [A] values and the slope is sensitive to them.
sources: Churchill-Bernstein / Churchill-Chu correlations; Sharqawy et al. 2010 seawater properties; TEOS-10 (gsw)
HYCOM GLBy0.08 expt 93.0 analysis, THREDDS NCSS (tds.hycom.org); a model, not observations
Argo float profiles, Ifremer ERDDAP ArgoFloats (erddap.ifremer.fr), QC flag 1

drake.title: Can the hull reject 0.96 MW?
drake.assumption: Hull area x1.5 (U = 200 + 1200 v) rejects the full pod load at a normal 22 to 32 C loop
drake.finding: To reject 0.96 MW with the x1.5 hull (fins at 85% efficiency) at this site's weakest-current case (P5, 0.05 m/s), the coolant supply must be 20.0 C; at the median current 19.2 C. The sim's own U would say 17.0 C. Full-power operation without throttling needs a supply of 27 C or less (chip model Tj = coolant + 38 K, throttle at 70 C); the vendor maximum is 32 C.
drake.sim_change: If the needed supply is above 27 C, add area (target bare-hull factor of about 1.3 before fin efficiency) or plan on throttling during weak-current periods.
sources: Churchill-Bernstein / Churchill-Chu correlations; Sharqawy et al. 2010 seawater properties; TEOS-10 (gsw)
HYCOM GLBy0.08 expt 93.0 analysis, THREDDS NCSS (tds.hycom.org); a model, not observations
Argo float profiles, Ifremer ERDDAP ArgoFloats (erddap.ifremer.fr), QC flag 1

drake.title: Bulk warming of the water passing a pod
drake.assumption: 0.03 K for one pod at 0.2 m/s; 10 pods in the same stream add linearly
drake.finding: Ten in-line pods warm the passing water by 0.39 K at the median current and 1.22 K at P95; it exceeds the 0.5 K illustrative limit 33.1% of the time. Values below 0.02 m/s are floored there, where the real plume turns buoyant and rises instead of diluting.
drake.sim_change: Stagger pods across the stream (cross-flow spacing) so no pod sits in another's wake, and agree a real ecological limit with the ecology team.
sources: HYCOM GLBy0.08 expt 93.0 analysis, THREDDS NCSS (tds.hycom.org); a model, not observations

drake.title: Hub-height wind resource
drake.finding: MERRA-2 gives a mean of 12.6 m/s at 150 m (shear exponent 0.115 fitted from 10 m and 50 m, extrapolated), 2.1 m/s above the 10.5 m/s base case. Weibull k fits at 2.82 (sim 2.2). Capacity factor per turbine 72% with the capex model's power curve and 10% losses. Cross-check: ERA5 100 m is +2.0% against MERRA-2 over 8 common years (hourly correlation 0.95).
drake.sim_change: Use 12.6 m/s as this site's base wind. Reanalyses smooth gusts and wakes, and the 50 m to 150 m extrapolation adds uncertainty, so treat it as slightly optimistic.
sources: NASA POWER hourly WS10M and WS50M, MERRA-2 reanalysis (power.larc.nasa.gov)
ECMWF ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive API (archive-api.open-meteo.com)

drake.title: Wind gaps: share of load served at 2x overbuild + 12 h storage
drake.assumption: Synthetic Weibull + AR(1, rho 0.985) wind, served fraction from the capex model
drake.finding: With real hourly wind the 2x/12 h design serves 94.4% of the load, against 84.0% for the synthetic series at the same mean (10.4 points more). Years vary from 91.5% to 97.0%. Longest stretch below 5 m/s is 57 h in reality versus 174 h synthetic. The capex base case (synthetic, 10.5 m/s mean) serves 77.9%. A 90% served fraction needs only 1.4x overbuild with 12 h storage here.
drake.sim_change: Replace the synthetic wind in capex_model.py with this site's ERA5 series; use the served_grid to re-pick overbuild and storage.
sources: ECMWF ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive API (archive-api.open-meteo.com)

drake.title: Sea state for pod swaps (72 h windows)
drake.assumption: An annual service/recovery campaign is possible (capex model: $8M/yr)
drake.finding: Median significant wave height is 3.5 m and the 99th percentile 7.6 m (max 12.4 m). A 72 h window with Hs under 2.5 m is open 0.5% of hours over the year and 1.6% in the best three months (month 6).
drake.sim_change: Budget weather standby days in the campaign cost, size the work for Hs 3 m or more with a DP vessel, or shorten the swap procedure below 72 h.
sources: Open-Meteo marine archive, wave model reanalysis from April 2021 (marine-api.open-meteo.com)

drake.title: Cost per GPU-hour with real wind
drake.assumption: Base case: $5.66 per sold GPU-hour (synthetic wind, 2x overbuild, 12 h storage), terrestrial $2.61
drake.finding: With this site's real wind the base design costs $4.71 per sold GPU-hour (-17% against the capex base case $5.66) because it serves 94% instead of 79%. Re-optimised (1.5x overbuild, 12 h storage) it reaches $4.59, -19% against base and +76% against terrestrial ($2.61). Everything else in the capex model is unchanged.
drake.sim_change: Feed each site's wind series into capex_model.py and re-pick overbuild and storage; wind capex and storage are the levers that move.
sources: NASA POWER hourly WS10M and WS50M, MERRA-2 reanalysis (power.larc.nasa.gov)

chile.finding: MERRA-2 gives a mean of 13.7 m/s at 150 m (shear exponent 0.089 fitted from 10 m and 50 m, extrapolated), 3.2 m/s above the 10.5 m/s base case. Weibull k fits at 2.87 (sim 2.2). Capacity factor per turbine 74% with the capex model's power curve and 10% losses. Cross-check: ERA5 100 m is +1.6% against MERRA-2 over 4 common years (hourly correlation 0.96).
chile.sim_change: Use 13.7 m/s as this site's base wind. Reanalyses smooth gusts and wakes, and the 50 m to 150 m extrapolation adds uncertainty, so treat it as slightly optimistic.
sources: NASA POWER hourly WS10M and WS50M, MERRA-2 reanalysis (power.larc.nasa.gov)
ECMWF ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive API (archive-api.open-meteo.com)

chile.title: Wind gaps: share of load served at 2x overbuild + 12 h storage
chile.assumption: Synthetic Weibull + AR(1, rho 0.985) wind, served fraction from the capex model
chile.finding: With real hourly wind the 2x/12 h design serves 94.4% of the load, against 85.2% for the synthetic series at the same mean (9.2 points more). Years vary from 91.1% to 96.3%. Longest stretch below 5 m/s is 107 h in reality versus 134 h synthetic. The capex base case (synthetic, 10.5 m/s mean) serves 77.9%. A 90% served fraction needs only 1.3x overbuild with 12 h storage here.
chile.sim_change: Replace the synthetic wind in capex_model.py with this site's ERA5 series; use the served_grid to re-pick overbuild and storage.
sources: ECMWF ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive API (archive-api.open-meteo.com)

chile.title: Sea state for pod swaps (72 h windows)
chile.assumption: An annual service/recovery campaign is possible (capex model: $8M/yr)
chile.finding: Median significant wave height is 4.2 m and the 99th percentile 8.1 m (max 10.7 m). A 72 h window with Hs under 2.5 m is open 0.6% of hours over the year and 1.4% in the best three months (month 7).
chile.sim_change: Budget weather standby days in the campaign cost, size the work for Hs 3 m or more with a DP vessel, or shorten the swap procedure below 72 h.
sources: Open-Meteo marine archive, wave model reanalysis from April 2021 (marine-api.open-meteo.com)

chile.title: Cost per GPU-hour with real wind
chile.assumption: Base case: $5.66 per sold GPU-hour (synthetic wind, 2x overbuild, 12 h storage), terrestrial $2.61
chile.finding: With this site's real wind the base design costs $4.71 per sold GPU-hour (-17% against the capex base case $5.66) because it serves 94% instead of 79%. Re-optimised (1.25x overbuild, 4 h storage) it reaches $4.52, -20% against base and +73% against terrestrial ($2.61). Everything else in the capex model is unchanged.
chile.sim_change: Feed each site's wind series into capex_model.py and re-pick overbuild and storage; wind capex and storage are the levers that move.
sources: NASA POWER hourly WS10M and WS50M, MERRA-2 reanalysis (power.larc.nasa.gov)
